title: Monster Realm — RED, SLOs & saturation
description: M20 operational dashboard (ADR-0180). Every panel queries either a recorded mr:* series from ops/observability/rules/recording.rules.yml or a raw host-native spacetime_*/up series — checkQueriedSeriesAreDefined enforces that closure, so no panel can reference a series nothing emits.

list.name: slo_set
list.label: SLO reducer set
list.description: OBS-22 — DERIVED from the recording rule's own matcher (the single source of truth), never a second hand-maintained copy of the allowlist.

panels.title: Reducer success SLO ($slo_set)
panels.description: OBS-22/OBS-23 — computed ONLY over the named allowlist. committed="false" conflates a real reducer failure with a guard correctly rejecting a bad request, so guard rejections are a separate panel below and are never blended into this ratio.

panels.title: $slo_set membership — transaction rate by reducer
panels.description: OBS-22 — the allowlist made visible. These are exactly the reducers the SLO above is computed over.

panels.title: Guard rejection rate (NOT a failure)
panels.description: OBS-23 — sourced from S2's evt:"reject" log lines (guards::log_reject, shipping today). A rising line here means the guards are working, not that the server is broken; that is precisely why it is kept out of the success ratio.

panels.title: Movement tick p95 vs STEP_MS
panels.description: OBS-24 — the movement-tick latency SLO: p95 must stay under STEP_MS (game-core/src/world.rs: STEP_MS = 200ms = 0.2s). Crossing this line is also mr-load-driver's definition of the measured breaking point (OBS-27).

panels.title: Client FPS p50 (SLO >= 55)
panels.description: OBS-25 — sourced ONLY from S4 browser metrics. Reads 0 until m20c (client OTel Web SDK) ships and starts emitting mr_client_fps.

panels.title: Saturation — subscription send queue
panels.description: OBS-26 early warning. Monotonic growth here is the other breaking-point signal mr-load-driver watches (OBS-27).

panels.title: Meta — Alloy liveness AND ingest throughput
panels.description: OBS-39 plus its pipeline-health companion. `up` alone only proves Alloy's HTTP server answers; a stalled file tail leaves up=1 while S2 ingestion is entirely dark, so both series are shown together (ADR-0180 amendment, Correction 3).

panels.title: Module heartbeat rate (m20a contract — unverified until m20e)
panels.description: The `heartbeat` half of the D6 evt vocabulary. mr_log/mr_heartbeat are m20a's and m20a may still adjust the envelope before merging; per M20 §5's own mitigation, drift is caught by m20e's post-merge integration eval, not by any pre-merge check. Reads 0 until m20a ships.

panels.title: RESERVED — chat flood (M19)
panels.description: OBS-28 — chat-flood load scenarios stay a reserved panel until M19 (chat) exists, and M20 completion does NOT depend on them. This is a real query against a real recorded series that legitimately reads zero today and lights up the moment chat emits events — a reservation, not a fabricated number.

panels.title: Scheduled-function lateness (share of starts over the 50 ms bucket edge)
panels.description: Share of scheduled-function starts that began MORE than 50 ms after their due time, per function, over 5m. This is an over-edge ratio at a REAL bucket edge of spacetime_scheduled_function_delay_seconds, not a quantile: on the measured 2.8.1 lattice p95 sits inside the (0.001, 0.005] bucket while the starts that matter are in the far tail (some over 60s), so p95 reads healthy straight through an excursion. The host's own late-start log::warn! fires at 30 ms — that is a Loki-side log threshold, not a bucket edge of this histogram, so it is not the number drawn here. The red line is the same 0.01 the ScheduledFunctionDelayed alert evaluates. See rules/recording.rules.yml (group mr-scheduler) for the full numbered provenance.
